problems.memo_sentence: The authors state that their QSVT-based state preparation achieves circuit depth scaling as O(d n), i.e., linear in the number of counterparties for fixed polynomial degree d, in contrast to earlier exponential-growth constructions.
problems.source_evidence: “The depth of Q scales as O(dn). Thus, for a fixed d, our method achieves linear scaling with respect to the number of counterparties n. The independence of d from n remains to be proved and will be analyzed in future works.”
problems.explanation: The memo presents the linear scaling as an established result without preserving the explicit caveat that it only holds for fixed d and that the independence of d from n is unproven.

problems.memo_sentence: The paper claims as its main contribution a novel end-to-end implementation of a quantum algorithm for VaR estimation in credit risk that uses amplitude loading and QSVT to avoid costly arithmetic while achieving improved, nominally linear scaling in the number of counterparties.
problems.source_evidence: “Our primary innovation builds on the extension proposed in [16], [17]... In this work, we propose an amplitude loading approach...”
problems.explanation: The memo attributes the broader multivariate credit-risk framework and the prior exponential-scaling issue as if they were original claims of this paper, but the paper explicitly says these build on and extend [16], [17].

problems.memo_sentence: The experimental evaluation is conducted entirely in simulation, benchmarking quantum-estimated CDF values and VaR against classical reconstructions from the same underlying dataset, which supports correctness but does not address hardware noise or real-time performance.
problems.source_evidence: The Results/Conclusion sections also state: “The simulation results validate the effectiveness of our methodology... These findings represent a step closer towards the possibility of efficiently realizing practical quantum risk analysis on quantum computers.”
problems.explanation: The memo captures the simulation-only nature of the experiments, but it underemphasizes the paper’s actual results/discussion framing, which includes the specific convergence behavior and the stated future-work limitations on scaling and T-depth analysis.
